simulation_metadata.version: 2.2 — chemical/geomagnetic/orbital domains, plus generated series and species inventory

provenance.note: projected_time_series and threshold_crossings are GENERATED, not hand-authored. Re-run reproduce.py after any model change and commit the diff. Two successive hand-authored revisions of this series failed to reproduce from the model they were attributed to (RESEARCH_LOG H-01, H-14) — that is why this block exists.

atmospheric_parameters.al2o3_residence_time_note: Corrected from 30yr; based on meteor smoke particle transport
atmospheric_parameters.al2o3_residence_time_conflict: CONTESTED. Ferreira et al. 2024 — the source of the 30 kg/satellite yield used in this same model — describes Al2O3 taking up to 30 years to settle from the top of the mesosphere into the ozone layer. That is 6x this value and scales steady-state burden almost proportionally. Unresolved: see RESEARCH_LOG.md H-13. reproduce.py reports both.
atmospheric_parameters.coupling_resonance_note: Removed. Proton gyrofrequency ~760 Hz, electron ~1.4 MHz; previous 100 MHz value was incorrect by ~5 orders of magnitude. This closes RESEARCH_LOG U-4.

risk_thresholds._note: chi_max of each regime is the floor of the next. The 2025-12-16 config gave cascade_failure a chi_limit of 5.0 while the model code labelled cascade at 3.0, leaving 3.0-5.0 unassigned. Resolved by naming that band Pre-Cascade rather than by redefining either boundary. See RESEARCH_LOG.md H-05.

chemical_parameters.so2_enhancement_note: Multiplicative increase in gamma when SO2 is adsorbed on Al2O3 surfaces
chemical_parameters.mechanism_note: Ferreira et al. 2024 report that Al2O3 does not react with ozone directly — it activates chlorine and is not consumed. Any direct-catalysis rate here is therefore incomplete: the chlorine supply, largely from solid rocket motors, is co-limiting and is not modelled. See RESEARCH_LOG.md H-12.
chemical_parameters.confidence: MEDIUM for catalysis rates, LOW for SAI synergy magnitude

geomagnetic_parameters.confidence: HIGH for field evolution, LOW for EPP-particle coupling

orbital_parameters.note: Natural meteoric Al2O3 (~400 t/yr) >> current satellite Al2O3 (~22 t/yr) but chemically distinct
orbital_parameters.context_note: Baseline offset, NOT a competing source. The satellite contribution ADDS to this population, so any threshold is reached sooner than a satellite-only model shows, not later. Two consequences. (1) At 5-yr residence the natural steady-state burden is ~1,970 MT — roughly 2x the 1,000 MT critical_mass_threshold_mt — so that threshold cannot be an absolute total-burden figure; it would have been permanently crossed long before satellites existed. It must be an anthropogenic-excess threshold, a threshold on something other than bulk mass, or wrong (U-2). (2) Mass fraction is the wrong metric for a conductivity question: Murphy et al. 2023 find spacecraft metals inside the SAME sulfate particles as meteoric metals, making the anthropogenic material a dopant in an existing host population, and dopant effects on conductivity are not mass-weighted. Note also that the ~18x natural:satellite ratio is a 2025 snapshot: satellite flux grows 15%/yr against constant meteoric input and crosses over around 2046. See RESEARCH_LOG.md H-15.
orbital_parameters.confidence: HIGH for meteoric input, LOW for close-pass scenarios

species_inventory.note: Al2O3 is 1 of 13 known species, across 1 of 2 emission pathways. Every parameter in this file describes that one species on that one pathway.
